newsitem.title: USA: Prodigy not liable for woman contracting HIV.
newsitem.headline: Prodigy not liable for woman contracting HIV.

text.p: A federal judge Wednesday dismissed a case against Prodigy Services Co. brought by one of its customers who contracted the AIDS virus from sex with a Prodigy employee she met online.

Manhattan U.S. District Court Judge Sonia Sotomayor ruled that the employee's sexual relationship with the woman and his failure to disclose that he was HIV-positive were beyond the scope of his employment with the on-line service provider.
The suit claimed the employee was "a sexual predator" who, because he was a Prodigy employee, "was able to spend countless hours online with plaintiff while he was working at Prodigy's offices."

The man "gave plaintiff months of 'free time' on the Prodigy network, as well as unlimited use of his own Prodigy account ... to entice (her) by any means necessary into an illicit and aberrant sexual relationship," the suit said.
The woman claimed that Prodigy knew of his HIV status and "should have taken special precautions to prevent" his conduct.

Sotomayor said in her opinion that if she found Prodigy liable "I would be setting a precedent under which employers would be forced to monitor, and in some cases control, not only the health of their employees, but also the most intimate aspects of their off-duty lives."
